# BadBuilderLinux v2.4.0

Prepare a **Peer Pressure installer USB**, package Aurora and other homebrew for installation to the HDD, and choose Aurora as the default dashboard from BadBuilder.

## What's new

- **Exploit → Peer Pressure** downloads the official v1.0.477 `SoftmodInstaller.zip`, pinned to its exact release and upstream SHA-256, plus the Rock Band Blitz demo. The upstream installer, license, and bundled XeLL are preserved.
- **Homebrew** packages Aurora, XeXMenu, utilities, and custom apps through Peer Pressure's `SoftmodExtras.ini`. Existing catalog entries are retained, and homebrew does not replace the installer payload.
- **Set default dashboard → Aurora** adds the supported `DashXex` setting after verifying the executable exists. On the console, enable **Install Extras** and select **Aurora** to apply it. Use **Extras Only** for an existing Peer Pressure setup.
- Peer Pressure supplies its own payload and dashboard configuration. BadUpdate and ABadAvatar continue using their existing bootstrap and USB homebrew workflows.
- The README now covers downloads, workflow selection, Aurora setup after installation, recovery, and testing. A root changelog collects release history.

## Compatibility and backup

Peer Pressure supports Xenon, Zephyr, Falcon, Jasper, and Trinity consoles; **Corona and Winchester are unsupported**. It requires an HDD, with a mechanical SATA drive recommended. DashLaunch and its plugins are unsupported. Choose a dashboard such as Aurora for default startup; the picker also accepts executable maintenance utilities.

BadBuilder erases the selected USB. Peer Pressure installation on the console modifies NAND and HDD security sectors and can cause data loss or prevent booting. Create and keep the official installer's system backup outside the USB before reusing it. Follow the [official installation guide](https://github.com/grimdoomer/Xbox360PeerPressure/wiki/Installation).

## Validation

- 68 tests pass locally, covering the existing safety checks and Peer Pressure installer, extras, default-dashboard paths, and INI injection handling.
- The real upstream installer and built-in homebrew archives pass extraction, complete-plan installation into a temporary directory, copied-file hash comparison, and Aurora configuration checks.
- Linux and Windows self-contained builds have been checked; the release workflow builds and tests both platforms before publishing.
- Aurora default-dashboard startup has been confirmed on one physical setup. Broader console/HDD compatibility testing remains outstanding.

## Downloads

- `BadBuilder-linux-x64` — self-contained Linux x64 binary
- `BadBuilder-win-x64.exe` — self-contained Windows x64 binary
- `SHA256SUMS` — checksums for both binaries

On Linux, make the binary executable and run it without sudo. The previous v2.3.1 binaries remain available for earlier USB preparation workflows.
